algorithm.title: General Approach to Children and Adolescents with Suspected ADHD.

cell.label: You suspect ADHD because of inattention, hyperactivity, impulsivity, academic underachievement, or behavior problems. Situational crisis?
Use Vanderbilt screening tool (http://www.nichq.org/adhd_tools.html) along with evaluating DSM-V criteria for ADHD.
Check home and school environment; consider counseling, referral, or other diagnoses.
Screen for other primary disorders and associated comorbidities (if present, consider neuropsychiatric testing).
Educate child, parent, and school; determine goals for therapy; regular physical activity; pharmacotherapy; focused counseling for child and parent may be needed; support groups (eg, CHADD).
Educate child, parent, and school; learning disorder may require accommodations; advocacy group (eg, CHADD); depending on complexity of comorbidities, may consult psychiatrist or psychologist.
Treat underlying condition. May require subspecialist referral.

algorithm.title: General Approach to Adults with Suspected ADHD.

cell.label: You suspect ADHD because of inattention, impulsivity and/or hyperactivity leading to pervasive impairment. Significant crisis?
Consider other etiology; ie, substance abuse, head trauma.
Is patient in school or going back to school, or in a profession where the possible use of a controlled substance needs to be documented?
Suggest neuropsychological testing and/or psychiatric consult if there's concern about any comorbidity.
Educate patient and family about disorder; daily exercise; pharmacotherapy; specialized counseling for comorbid issues or behavioral problems; participate in advocacy and support groups.
